Derive a Key from a Password with PBKDF2

Source: R/kdf.R
crypt_pbkdf2.Rd

crypt_pbkdf2() stretches a password into a key with PBKDF2 (RFC 8018, section 5.2), using HMAC with the chosen digest as the pseudorandom function.

Usage

crypt_pbkdf2(password, salt, iterations, length = 32, algorithm = "sha256")

Arguments

password

The password, as a raw vector. A string is not accepted, because its bytes depend on an encoding: convert deliberately, for example with charToRaw(enc2utf8(x)). It may be empty.

salt

The salt, as a raw vector. Use at least 16 random bytes from crypt_rand_bytes(), a fresh salt for each password. It may be empty, which only interoperability with an existing format justifies.

iterations

The iteration count, a whole number from 1 to 4294967295. It has no default, because the right value depends on the digest, the hardware and the time you can afford. OWASP recommended 600,000 for "sha256" in 2023.

length

The number of bytes to derive, a whole number of at least 1. 32 gives an AES-256 key.

algorithm

The digest for the HMAC: "sha256" (the default), "sha384", "sha512" or "sha1". "sha1" is for formats that specify it, never for anything new.

Value

A raw vector of length bytes.

Details

PBKDF2 derives a key. It is not an encryption format and not a password storage format. The salt, the iteration count and the digest are yours to choose, store beside what the key protects, and supply again to derive the same key.

Cost

The time is proportional to iterations times the number of digest-sized blocks in length, and the call cannot be interrupted. Bound iterations before passing a value that came from untrusted input, such as a file header.

Errors

An invalid argument is zucrypt_invalid_argument, and an unknown digest is zucrypt_unsupported_algorithm.

See also

crypt_aes_gcm_encrypt(), which takes the key this derives.

Examples

salt <- crypt_rand_bytes(16)
key <- crypt_pbkdf2(charToRaw("correct horse"), salt, iterations = 10000)
key
#>  [1] 06 bd ca 83 7e ca 9d ca 5f f8 eb cb 8a c8 87 e7 a5 7c 9a ad ba db b0 5e c8
#> [26] a4 18 01 15 e0 44 29

# RFC 6070, test case 2.
crypt_hex(crypt_pbkdf2(charToRaw("password"), charToRaw("salt"),
                       iterations = 2, length = 20, algorithm = "sha1"))
#> [1] "ea6c014dc72d6f8ccd1ed92ace1d41f0d8de8957"
